title: "Recitation": the name
hook: the word means recitation: it was spoken before it was written

segments.voice: Yesterday, the heart's polish: the heart as a mirror, and remembrance as the cloth. Your line was polish the heart. Did you wipe one film away? That closed the Sufi path. Today a new strand begins. Day three hundred nine.

A parent at bedtime, doing all the voices. A friend reading a message out loud, in a funny accent. Words change when someone says them. They get a speed, a breath, a face behind them. Now: the book at the center of Islam. Its name is easy to say, and its meaning is easy to miss. That name isn't a word for something written. It's a word for something spoken. For the next three weeks, we look at how the Qur'an is built: its parts, its verses, its scribes and its reciters. Today, the name itself.
screen: `WORDS SOUND DIFFERENT IN A VOICE.` → `WHAT DOES THE NAME MEAN?` → `HOW THE QUR'AN IS BUILT.`

segments.voice: The word Qur'an comes from the Arabic root q, r, and a catch in the throat, which means to read aloud, to recite. Qur'an is recitation, or the thing that is recited. You've met this root before. The first word the angel Jibril brought to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the cave of Hira came from it: iqra'. In Pickthall's words: "Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth." Read and recite are one word in Arabic. And that first revelation came, Muslims say, to a man who did not read or write. So from the very beginning, the Qur'an was heard before it was written. The Prophet recited what came to him. Companions heard it, repeated it and learned it by heart. Scribes wrote it down too, on whatever was at hand, but the living copy was in voices. The hadith collections say that every Ramadan, Jibril went over the Qur'an with the Prophet, recitation for recitation, and in his last year, twice. The Qur'an even tells him how: "chant the Qur'an in measured measure," in Pickthall's rendering of Surah 73. That's why a child's Qur'an lesson traditionally begins with listening to a teacher and repeating, not with silent reading. It's why the prayer, the call to prayer and the nights of Ramadan are full of recitation. The Qur'an also calls itself kitab, a writing, and Muslims hold both: a book you can hold, and a voice you can hear. But its own name leans toward the voice. When people say it doesn't feel the same on a silent page, this is part of what they mean. It was made to be said.
screen: `FROM THE ROOT: TO RECITE` · `IQRA': THE FIRST WORD` · `HEARD BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN` · `A BOOK AND A VOICE`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: recite something aloud. If you know al-Fatiha, or any short surah from the juz' you walked through, say it now, out loud, not in your head. Slowly. Hear what your voice does with it. If you're learning, say the one line you know best, even just bismillah, or read a line of anything you love at a speaking pace. Then sit in the quiet after it, and notice the words still hanging in the room. The bell holds the time.
Qur'an. Recitation: the thing that is recited, from the same root as iqra', read. Today's word.

Your line: the book is a voice. Today, read one thing aloud that you'd normally read silently, a verse, a poem, a message from someone you love, and notice what the voice adds. Day three hundred nine.

howItsDone: Muslims learn the Qur'an first by listening and repeating after a teacher, and recite it aloud in prayer, in Ramadan and at home; some say it is fully itself only when it is recited.

you listen to the teacher and repeat.
fork.reveal: the traditional first lesson is listen and repeat. the Qur'an was a voice before it was a page, and it's still taught that way.

original.note: Arabic: recitation, the thing recited. from the root of iqra', read.

trapdoor: what you thought: the name of the holy book of Islam.
what it means: recitation, the thing that is recited: a voice before a page.
what a scholar hears: the usual reading takes it as a verbal noun of qara'a, to read aloud; al-Shafi'i, by report, held it to be a proper name not taken from that root.
